scenario: AITA for saying "See you next year" to a teacher who is getting let go? | So this teacher (I will call him R) was new at my school this year. Immediately he tried to impose his own way of teaching and grading on us (the students) which was very different that anything we had ever experienced. You were expected to do things his way, and even if his was was wrong, which people pointed out to him, you were still expected to use it. R also took points off for scratch work that he didn't like, and tried to take off as many points as possible on the tests, quizzes, and homeworks. Every student he had with no exception was subjuct to this. R also took forever to grade our assignments. We took a test the week before spring break, and got it back ~6 weeks later. He also refused to go over it with anyone. R never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. The administration took notice and we were informed that R was not coming back next year. Needless to say, we were overjoyed about this. Since the announcement, R completely checked out, he just wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class,and went to Disneyland instead of going to one of the review days for exams. Yesterday, as I was walking out Of R's classroom for the last time, I called "See you next year!" over my shoulder. My friends have told me that I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. AITA?

First, I need to evaluate the morality of the action. The key points here are the teacher's behavior and the student's comment. The teacher was described as hostile, unhelpful, and unfair. The students were happy about his departure. The phrase "See you next year" is typically a friendly goodbye, but in this context, since the teacher isn't coming back, it might be seen as sarcastic or dismissive.

However, the student's intention might not have been malicious. They might have just been using a common phrase without thinking. The teacher's actions were clearly problematic, so the students' relief is understandable. The question is whether the comment was appropriate given the circumstances.

Morally, the action could be seen as acceptable if the student didn't intend to be hurtful. The teacher's behavior was so negative that the students' reaction is justified. However, the phrase "See you next year" might be inappropriate because the teacher isn't returning. It could be perceived as mocking or insincere. But since the teacher was let go due to his actions, maybe the students' comment is a reflection of their relief rather than malice.

Alternatively, if the comment was meant to be sarcastic, that could be seen as morally unacceptable. But without clear evidence of intent, it's a bit ambiguous. Considering the teacher's actions were so bad that the students were justified in their relief, the comment might be seen as a natural reaction. However, the specific phrase could be problematic. But in many cases, people use such phrases without ill intent. So, maybe the action is morally acceptable because the teacher's behavior warranted the students' reaction, and the comment wasn't necessarily malicious.
